currentContext.strengths: Integrated, end-to-end ash management platform spanning evacuation, transportation, utilization, logistics management and regulatory compliance, differentiating Refex from standalone transportation providers|Long-term framework and partnership relationships with leading power utilities, including NTPC and state GENCOs|Exclusive technology licensing partnership with Vensys Energy AG providing access to Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) wind-turbine technology|Proprietary technology platform in the mobility business (RGML) covering automated dispatch, real-time fleet and battery monitoring, and smart route planning
currentContext.strategies: Shift from an execution-led ash logistics provider to a strategic, integrated solutions partner for power utilities, covering evacuation, transportation, utilization, logistics management and regulatory compliance end-to-end|Deepen long-term framework/partnership relationships with leading power utilities to improve customer integration and visibility|In Wind Energy, scale manufacturing capacity, strengthen the domestic supply-chain ecosystem, and leverage the Vensys Energy AG technology partnership to build a competitive and resilient business|In Mobility, expand market presence and steer the business toward profitability while positioning as a premium, reliable, technology-driven mobility partner|Continue investing in AI-based solutions, digital platforms and data-driven decision-making across all businesses to build a more agile, technology-led organization|Digitalize core operations: implemented an end-to-end ERP platform across the Ash & Coal business integrated with mobile applications for real-time data capture; Venwind deployed SolidWorks/PLM enterprise platforms for design and document control; Mobility continued investing in its proprietary technology platform|Strengthen cybersecurity and infrastructure resilience (Sentinel platform, dual connectivity, firewall protection, network redundancy) to support the Company's next phase of growth|Pursue a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement among Refex Industries Limited (Demerged Company), Refex Green Mobility Limited (Transferor Company) and Refex Mobility Limited (Resulting Company), to create a separately listed mobility entity|Maintain a governance and sustainability-led approach to growth, with continued focus on transparency, accountability and responsible value creation as the Company enters its next growth phase
currentContext.expansion: Refex's capital expansion during FY26 centered on scaling its newly entered Wind Energy vertical: subsidiary Venwind Refex Power Limited manufactures 5.3 MW wind turbines under an exclusive Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) technology license from Vensys Energy AG, and during the year commissioned its Rotor and Nacelle Assembly facility at Silvassa (exact annual capacity figure not clearly legible in source text). Venwind is targeting a further increase in annual production capacity over the next five years and is developing a domestic supply chain through partnerships with global component manufacturers that have production capabilities in India, aimed at enhancing manufacturing resilience and supporting scalable production. In Ash Utilization & Coal Handling, the Company implemented an integrated ERP platform (a digital rather than physical capacity expansion) and, per BRSR disclosure, directed 30.22% of FY26 capital expenditure toward technologies that improve environmental and social impact, including equipment to enhance ash-disposal efficiency and the purchase of EV and CNG+petrol vehicles (versus 72.33% in FY25). In Mobility, Refex Green Mobility Limited continued to build out its EV-based fleet and proprietary technology platform (automated dispatch, fleet/battery monitoring, route planning) across Bengaluru, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR.
currentContext.mdna: Ash Handling expected to become increasingly critical as India's power demand grows and regulations around sustainable/100% ash utilization continue to strengthen, creating opportunities in integrated ash management, ancillary services and product-based avenues linked to the ash value chain|Coal is expected to remain a cornerstone of India's energy mix over the medium term, supporting continued demand for coal handling and logistics services|Wind-turbine demand driven by India's growing electricity requirements and expanding renewable-energy infrastructure, with green-energy open-access arrangements widening the customer base beyond traditional utilities to commercial, industrial and captive consumers, plus hybrid/storage projects and repowering of older wind farms|India's corporate mobility sector is shifting decisively toward reliable, compliant, technology-enabled and clean-fuel solutions, a trend management believes its mobility business is well aligned to address|Broader economy: India remains among the fastest-growing major economies with resilient domestic demand and rising infrastructure investment; higher fuel prices and energy-security concerns are expected to drive continued adoption of electric vehicles for logistics and fleet operations, though pace depends on vehicle economics, financing availability and charging infrastructure|Venwind secured orders from leading Independent Power Producers and built a wind-turbine order pipeline/order book during its first full year of operations (exact order volumes and values not clearly legible in source text).

risks.risk: Concentration in Ash & Coal Handling, which remains dependent on continued coal-based thermal power generation
risks.note: Ash & Coal Handling continued to be the Company's principal business segment; the business model depends on ongoing thermal power generation, ash-utilisation regulation, and relationships with a relatively concentrated set of large power producers (IPPs/CPPs, NTPC, state GENCOs).

risks.risk: Recent discontinuation of the Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas businesses
risks.note: The Company discontinued its Power Trading & Refrigerant business during the year (relatively low-margin), which changed the revenue base and reflects a history of active portfolio restructuring that could recur.

Venwind Refex Power Limited only commenced revenue contribution in FY26 (its first full year of active execution), and its growth depends on converting a confirmed order book of over 400 MW into executed, revenue-generating projects.

risks.risk: Asset- and fleet-intensive ash-handling execution platform
risks.note: The ash management business depends on an execution platform of over 2,500 owned and leased vehicles capable of handling more than 70,000 MT of ash per day; disruptions to fleet availability, logistics, or utilisation could affect service delivery.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the proposed mobility demerger
risks.note: The proposed demerger of the mobility business (into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited) had achieved approvals from stock exchanges and lenders during the year but remained subject to further regulatory/shareholder approvals and implementation risk.

risks.risk: New-vertical customer concentration in Premium Corporate Mobility
risks.note: The mobility business (RGML) serves a diversified but still developing customer base of multinational corporations and large domestic enterprises across five metro markets (Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi NCR); loss of large corporate clients or slower formalisation of the corporate mobility market could affect growth.

thesis (one line): Refex has structurally re-shaped from a low-margin **trading** house (refrigerant gases + power trading, both now exited) into a **service/logistics-led** business anchored by India's largest **coal & ash handling** franchise, with **wind WTG (Venwind)** entering active execution and the **EV/mobility** arm being demerged — driving a sharp margin re-rate (FY26 EBITDA margin 17.2% vs 9.2% prior) despite headline revenue degrowth.
scorecard (standalone, continuing operat:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 701 cr | INR 594 cr | **+18%** | Driven by Coal & Ash execution scaling |
| EBITDA | INR 141 cr | INR 62 cr | **+127%** | Mix shift to service business |
| EBITDA margin | **20.1%** | 10.4% | +970 bps | Product-mix (trading removed) |
| PAT | INR 94 cr | INR 56 cr | **+67%** | |
| PAT margin | 13.4% | ~9.4% | | |

| Metric (Full Year) | FY26 | FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 2,039 cr | INR 2,259 cr | **−10%** | Degrowth = ~INR 220 cr trading revenue (refrigerant gas + power trading) deliberately exited |
| EBITDA | INR 350 cr | INR 208 cr | **+68%** | |
| EBITDA margin | **17.2%** | ~9.2% | +800 bps | COGS down 18% vs revenue down 10%; manpower cost cut via technology |
| PAT | INR 247 cr | INR 184 cr | **+34%** | |
| PAT margin | 12.12% | ~8.1% | | |
| Ash & Coal segment (adj.) | — | — | **+28%** | Adjusted core growth ex-trading (mgmt: "28% to be precise") |
| Wind (Venwind) contribution | ~INR 233–238 cr | nil | new | Deliveries began Feb-2026 |

**One-offs / structural items:** (a) ~INR 2.0–2.2 cr finance-cost hit from refinancing/processing charges (moving from old to new bank for lower borrowing cost); (b) Refrigerant gas stock **fully liquidated**, residual receivable to close in current quarter; (c) Power trading **fully exited**; (d) Contract assets / unbilled revenue ~INR 700+ cr (running account, work done awaiting certification/billing); (e) Promoter warrants — non-subscription by promoter & non-promoter entity was a "deliberate decision" (no fundraise needed).
guidance (critical):
- **Coal & Ash Handling:** Same growth in FY27 as FY26 (i.e. **double-digit %** core growth); order pipeline **~INR 1,500 cr**. No capacity constraint — ramp is gradual, location-by-location.
- **Daily handling volume:** Currently **68,000–70,000 tons/day**; targeting ramp to **90,000–95,000 tons/day** (clarified this is a *future-year* target, achievable within current FY27, gradual).
- **Wind (Venwind):** Order book **INR 1,860 cr**; **INR 238 cr executed** in FY26 (Q4); **~INR 1,500 cr balance to be executed in FY27** → wind revenue could be **INR 1,700–1,800 cr** in FY27 (per analyst math, mgmt confirmed all old orders complete this year + possible new orders). "Massive growth" YoY on consol basis. Capacity target **~2 GW by next year-end**.
- **Margins:** Blended EBITDA margin guided **15–18%** sustainable (Q4's 20.1% described as sustainable, supported by service mix). Wind current EBITDA margin **~8%**, expected to *improve via localization* and to stay better than competitors. CFO: focus is to **maintain** current EBITDA margin given geopolitical uncertainty.
- **Net-profit guidance note:** Earlier "11–12%" guidance was on **PAT/net profit**, NOT EBITDA (clarification to analyst).
- **Capex/fundraise:** No immediate fundraise required for Refex Industries; sufficient internal accruals + bank limits.
order book / pipeline:
- **Coal & Ash:** ~INR 1,500 cr order pipeline; includes long-term contracts e.g. **APGENCO 3-year contract** (kicks in at start of FY); fresh orders ~INR 120–130 cr added in Q4. Operating across **40 thermal power plants** across India.
- **Wind (Venwind):** **INR 1,860 cr** firm order book; INR 238 cr executed; **~INR 1,500 cr open** for FY27. "Advanced stage" negotiations on a few more orders (not yet disclosable — earlier media chatter of ~INR 2,000 cr further pipeline NOT confirmed as firm).
segment detail:
- **Coal & Ash Handling (CORE):** India's largest organized player; integrated ash logistics + material handling + environmental-compliance. Coal-in / ash-out **reverse logistics** (rail "rack" mode or road) maximizes fleet utilization — hence coal vs ash revenue **cannot be split**. Escalation clauses cover **40–60%** of diesel cost (rest is a cost hit). TAM cited **~INR 75,000 cr**; Refex at ~INR 2,000 cr ≈ **3% share**. Nearest competitor estimated at ~25% of Refex's size; rest fragmented (1–5 plants each), none listed.
- **Wind / WTG (Venwind Refex Power):** German-licensed **5.3 MW turbine** platform; **ALMM approval received** in FY26 (key milestone); deliveries commenced Feb-2026, phased dispatch. Receivables backed by **LC** (short cycle, separate from standalone). EBITDA margin ~8% currently.
- **EV / Mobility (Refex Green Mobility):** Crossed **INR 100 cr revenue** in 3 years of operation; shifting to **asset-light** model with clean-fuel + enterprise-led scaling; progressing toward profitability. Being **demerged** (see below). Tailwind: PM's push to shift govt/agency fleets to EVs.
- **Refrigerant gases & Power trading:** Both **discontinued/exited** — refrigerant stock liquidated, residual receivable to close; power trading fully out.
growth / optionality:
- **Thermal-power structural tailwind:** ~**50 GW** new thermal capacity to be added in India over next 4–5 years; India coal consumption ~800 mn tons rising YoY. **Domestic coal ash content 37–40%** (vs imported 12–13%) → ash handling demand resilient regardless of coal imports. Coal gasification (syn-gas) program is **separate** and does NOT impact thermal/ash business.
- **Wind sector:** Structurally attractive — rising capacity-addition targets, stronger IPP participation, localization initiatives, improving policy visibility. Localization of components is the next 1–2 year margin lever.
- **EV mobility:** Optionality via demerger value-unlock + govt EV-shift policy.
- **Reclassification optionality:** Application filed (~2 months prior) to move out of "industrial gases" exchange classification → better peer comparability.
margins & cost: - Margin re-rate driven by **mix shift** (trading out, service in) — mgmt insists service margins were "always good." FY26: COGS −18% vs revenue −10%; manpower cost reduced via technology/automation. Diesel inflation only **40–60% pass-through**. Sustainable blended EBITDA **15–18%**; Q4 20.1% defended as sustainable.
capex: - No explicit capex number given. Wind capacity building toward ~2 GW; ash business is **asset-light** (works with partners). No immediate large capex/fundraise need.
capital allocation:
- **Underleveraged**; healthy debt-equity. Finance cost ~INR 30 cr FY26 (mostly working-capital driven; INR 2–2.2 cr one-off refinancing/processing charge). Refinancing underway at both Refex Industries and Venwind for lower borrowing cost. **No immediate fundraise** (promoter warrants deliberately not subscribed). **Demerger** of mobility to unlock value (different investor set for EV/sustainable vs core).
- **Promoter pledge:** ~**41%** (rose vs guidance to reduce). Mgmt: removal tied to loan closure (contractual); monthly payments ongoing; expects **partial/large-part removal over next ~6 months**.
risks:
- **Working-capital intensity:** Receivable days ~105–130 (mgmt guides 105–125 days steady); contract assets/unbilled ~INR 700+ cr — execution-to-cash lag a structural drag.
- **Diversification execution:** Three very different businesses (logistics services, heavy WTG manufacturing, EV mobility) — execution & capital-allocation complexity.
- **Promoter pledge at 41%** rose despite prior reduction guidance — credibility/overhang risk.
- **Diesel cost** only partially passed through (40–60%).
- **IT search / enforcement overhang** (raised by analyst) — mgmt says all disclosures done, no expected financial/reputational impact; one caller praised regaining "industrial confidence" post regulator/enforcement issues.
- **Wind order-pipeline guidance soft** — only INR 1,860 cr firm; further orders not yet signed.
- **Demerger timeline** subject to NCLT court process (~75–90 days, ~August 2026 expected); company-side compliances 100% done.
management tone: Confident, measured, repeatedly **refused to give numeric guidance** ("we'll have a good growth," "not speaking on any number"). Emphasis on **quality of profit/margin over revenue**, governance, and asset-light scaling. CMD Anil Jain notably "relaxed" vs prior calls (deliberately delegating Q&A to build leaders). Strong analyst sentiment / praise for management.
non-obvious points:
- Revenue "degrowth" is **deliberate de-risking** (exiting INR 220 cr low-margin trading), not demand loss — core ash grew 28%.
- Coal vs ash revenue split is **structurally impossible** due to reverse-logistics fleet optimization.
- Wind receivables are **LC-backed** → cleaner cash cycle than the working-capital-heavy ash business.
- "11–12%" prior guidance was **PAT margin**, not EBITDA — a recurring analyst misunderstanding.
- Imported-coal substitution does NOT hurt ash business (domestic coal ~3x ash content).
- Coal gasification (govt syn-gas program) is unrelated to thermal/ash demand.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **Refex itself** — primary beneficiary of structural thermal-power growth (50 GW new capacity), tightening ash/environmental-compliance norms, and India's largest organized ash-logistics moat (40 plants, proprietary logistics tech).
- ✅ Govt EV-shift policy → tailwind for the (to-be-demerged) **Refex Green Mobility**.
- ✅ Domestic wind capacity-addition / IPP push → tailwind for **Venwind** (ALMM-approved 5.3 MW platform).
- (Fragmented unorganized ash players remain the displaced incumbents.)

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Refex Industries is a diversified conglomerate anchored across Ash Utilization & Coal Handling, Green Mobility and Wind Energy, positioning itself as an integrated partner in India's clean-energy transition.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Refex Industries began in 2002 as a refrigerant-gas company and has since diversified into three core verticals: Ash Utilization & Coal Handling (ash evacuation, transportation, utilization and coal supply/logistics services for coal-based thermal power plants), Green Mobility (through wholly-owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Limited, offering EV-based employee transportation, corporate rentals and point-to-point travel for enterprises), and Wind Energy (through subsidiary Venwind Refex Power Limited, an original equipment manufacturer of wind turbines). It serves industrial customers such as power producers, cement manufacturers and infrastructure developers, largely within India.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Refex Holding Private Limited (formerly Sherisha Technologies Private Limited) — related party: Holding company (55.85% shareholder of RIL); counterparty for rental, interest and reimbursement transactions
- Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML) — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary operating the Refex Mobility EV-based mobility business
- Refex Mobility Limited (RML) — subsidiary: Wholly-owned (100%) subsidiary incorporated September 12, 2025; yet to commence operations; intended to become a separately listed mobility entity under a proposed Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement
- Refex EV Fleet Services Private Limited (formerly O3 Mobility Private Limited) — subsidiary: Step-down (wholly-owned) subsidiary of RGML; RIL holds it indirectly at 100%
- Venwind Refex Power Limited (VRPL) — subsidiary: Subsidiary (77.39% held) operating the wind-turbine OEM business under the Venwind brand
- Venwind Refex Power Services Limited (VRPSL) — subsidiary: Step-down (wholly-owned) subsidiary of VRPL; RIL holds it indirectly at 77.39%
- Refex Engineering Products Private Limited (REPPL) — subsidiary: Step-down (wholly-owned) subsidiary of VRPL, acquired December 5, 2025 from Refex Holding Private Limited via secondary transfer of equity shares; RIL holds it indirectly at 77.39%
- Venwind Refex Projects Limited — subsidiary: Step-down (wholly-owned) subsidiary of VRPL, incorporated November 25, 2025; RIL holds it indirectly at 77.39%
- Refex Renewables and Infrastructure Ltd (previously SunEdison Infrastructure Ltd) — related party: Entity in which Key Managerial Personnel are interested; counterparty for sales and rental transactions
- Sparzana Aviation Private Limited — related party: Firm in which Key Managerial Personnel are interested; counterparty for rental transactions
- Ugamdevi Tarachand Foundations — related party: Entity in which Key Managerial Personnel are interested; recipient of CSR expenditure
- Aabhuti Investment Fund Trust — related party: Entity in which Key Managerial Personnel are interested; counterparty for rental transactions

segment_detail.title: Segment Detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Coal & Ash Handling (CORE):** India's largest organized player; integrated ash logistics + material handling + environmental-compliance. Coal-in / ash-out **reverse logistics** (rail "rack" mode or road) maximizes fleet utilization — hence coal vs ash revenue **cannot be split**. Escalation clauses cover **40–60%** of diesel cost (rest is a cost hit). TAM cited **~INR 75,000 cr**; Refex at ~INR 2,000 cr ≈ **3% share**. Nearest competitor estimated at ~25% of Refex's size; rest fragmented (1–5 plants each), none listed.
- **Wind / WTG (Venwind Refex Power):** German-licensed **5.3 MW turbine** platform; **ALMM approval received** in FY26 (key milestone); deliveries commenced Feb-2026, phased dispatch. Receivables backed by **LC** (short cycle, separate from standalone). EBITDA margin ~8% currently.
- **EV / Mobility (Refex Green Mobility):** Crossed **INR 100 cr revenue** in 3 years of operation; shifting to **asset-light** model with clean-fuel + enterprise-led scaling; progressing toward profitability. Being **demerged** (see below). Tailwind: PM's push to shift govt/agency fleets to EVs.
- **Refrigerant gases & Power trading:** Both **discontinued/exited** — refrigerant stock liquidated, residual receivable to close; power trading fully out.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Ash Utilization & Coal Handling:** ash evacuation and transportation, ash utilization solutions (cement manufacturing, roads/infrastructure, mine filling), coal supply and logistics services
- **Mobility (Refex Green Mobility Limited / Refex Mobility):** EV-based employee transportation, corporate rentals, ad-hoc and point-to-point travel services
- **Wind Energy (Venwind Refex Power Limited):** 5.3 MW wind turbines, turbines using Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) technology under exclusive license from Vensys Energy AG

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- thermal power producers (IPPs and CPPs) including NTPC and state GENCOs
- cement manufacturers
- road and infrastructure developers
- mining sector (mine filling)
- enterprise mobility customers across Bengaluru, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR
- India (14 states served; exports under 1% of turnover; no international plants/offices)

order_book.title: Order Book / Pipeline
order_book.body:
- **Coal & Ash:** ~INR 1,500 cr order pipeline; includes long-term contracts e.g. **APGENCO 3-year contract** (kicks in at start of FY); fresh orders ~INR 120–130 cr added in Q4. Operating across **40 thermal power plants** across India.
- **Wind (Venwind):** **INR 1,860 cr** firm order book; INR 238 cr executed; **~INR 1,500 cr open** for FY27. "Advanced stage" negotiations on a few more orders (not yet disclosable — earlier media chatter of ~INR 2,000 cr further pipeline NOT confirmed as firm).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **Coal & Ash Handling:** Same growth in FY27 as FY26 (i.e. **double-digit %** core growth); order pipeline **~INR 1,500 cr**. No capacity constraint — ramp is gradual, location-by-location.
- **Daily handling volume:** Currently **68,000–70,000 tons/day**; targeting ramp to **90,000–95,000 tons/day** (clarified this is a *future-year* target, achievable within current FY27, gradual).
- **Wind (Venwind):** Order book **INR 1,860 cr**; **INR 238 cr executed** in FY26 (Q4); **~INR 1,500 cr balance to be executed in FY27** → wind revenue could be **INR 1,700–1,800 cr** in FY27 (per analyst math, mgmt confirmed all old orders complete this year + possible new orders). "Massive growth" YoY on consol basis. Capacity target **~2 GW by next year-end**.
- **Margins:** Blended EBITDA margin guided **15–18%** sustainable (Q4's 20.1% described as sustainable, supported by service mix). Wind current EBITDA margin **~8%**, expected to *improve via localization* and to stay better than competitors. CFO: focus is to **maintain** current EBITDA margin given geopolitical uncertainty.
- **Net-profit guidance note:** Earlier "11–12%" guidance was on **PAT/net profit**, NOT EBITDA (clarification to analyst).
- **Capex/fundraise:** No immediate fundraise required for Refex Industries; sufficient internal accruals + bank limits.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / Optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Thermal-power structural tailwind:** ~**50 GW** new thermal capacity to be added in India over next 4–5 years; India coal consumption ~800 mn tons rising YoY. **Domestic coal ash content 37–40%** (vs imported 12–13%) → ash handling demand resilient regardless of coal imports. Coal gasification (syn-gas) program is **separate** and does NOT impact thermal/ash business.
- **Wind sector:** Structurally attractive — rising capacity-addition targets, stronger IPP participation, localization initiatives, improving policy visibility. Localization of components is the next 1–2 year margin lever.
- **EV mobility:** Optionality via demerger value-unlock + govt EV-shift policy.
- **Reclassification optionality:** Application filed (~2 months prior) to move out of "industrial gases" exchange classification → better peer comparability.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ash Handling expected to become increasingly critical as India's power demand grows and regulations around sustainable/100% ash utilization continue to strengthen, creating opportunities in integrated ash management, ancillary services and product-based avenues linked to the ash value chain
- Coal is expected to remain a cornerstone of India's energy mix over the medium term, supporting continued demand for coal handling and logistics services
- Wind-turbine demand driven by India's growing electricity requirements and expanding renewable-energy infrastructure, with green-energy open-access arrangements widening the customer base beyond traditional utilities to commercial, industrial and captive consumers, plus hybrid/storage projects and repowering of older wind farms
- India's corporate mobility sector is shifting decisively toward reliable, compliant, technology-enabled and clean-fuel solutions, a trend management believes its mobility business is well aligned to address
- Broader economy: India remains among the fastest-growing major economies with resilient domestic demand and rising infrastructure investment; higher fuel prices and energy-security concerns are expected to drive continued adoption of electric vehicles for logistics and fleet operations, though pace depends on vehicle economics, financing availability and charging infrastructure
- Venwind secured orders from leading Independent Power Producers and built a wind-turbine order pipeline/order book during its first full year of operations (exact order volumes and values not clearly legible in source text).

margins.title: Margins & Cost
margins.body: - Margin re-rate driven by **mix shift** (trading out, service in) — mgmt insists service margins were "always good." FY26: COGS −18% vs revenue −10%; manpower cost reduced via technology/automation. Diesel inflation only **40–60% pass-through**. Sustainable blended EBITDA **15–18%**; Q4 20.1% defended as sustainable.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Refex's capital expansion during FY26 centered on scaling its newly entered Wind Energy vertical: subsidiary Venwind Refex Power Limited manufactures 5.3 MW wind turbines under an exclusive Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) technology license from Vensys Energy AG, and during the year commissioned its Rotor and Nacelle Assembly facility at Silvassa (exact annual capacity figure not clearly legible in source text). Venwind is targeting a further increase in annual production capacity over the next five years and is developing a domestic supply chain through partnerships with global component manufacturers that have production capabilities in India, aimed at enhancing manufacturing resilience and supporting scalable production. In Ash Utilization & Coal Handling, the Company implemented an integrated ERP platform (a digital rather than physical capacity expansion) and, per BRSR disclosure, directed 30.22% of FY26 capital expenditure toward technologies that improve environmental and social impact, including equipment to enhance ash-disposal efficiency and the purchase of EV and CNG+petrol vehicles (versus 72.33% in FY25). In Mobility, Refex Green Mobility Limited continued to build out its EV-based fleet and proprietary technology platform (automated dispatch, fleet/battery monitoring, route planning) across Bengaluru, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] RGML merges into RIL and RGML's shares held by RIL are cancelled; the mobility undertaking is then carved out of RIL into a new company, Refex Mobility Limited (RML), which will issue shares to all RIL shareholders at a 1:1 swap ratio and be listed as an independent entity — the stated rationale being "focused growth, value unlocking, and independent balance sheets across two differentiated business platforms".
- [Demerger status] BSE, NSE and lender approvals received; NCLT approval received for convening stakeholder meetings, with the Equity Shareholders' Meeting scheduled for 5 August 2026 and all scheme-related notices issued.
- [Regulation] MoEF & CC initial-cycle compliance deadlines vary by current utilization — 3 years if >80%, 4 years if 60-80%, 5 years if <60% — with mandatory cleanup of accumulated ash stocks effective from 1 April 2022.
- [Policy tailwind — wind] India's installed wind capacity ~50 GW (as of March 2025), 4th globally; MNRE wind capacity target of 140-150 GW by 2030; 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity target; domestic manufacturing capacity 18+ GW p.a.; GST on wind equipment reduced from 12% to 5%; updated national climate targets set 60% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2035.
- [Ownership] Promoter & Promoter Group holding rose from 53.33% (Sep-25) to 56.56% (Jun-26); FIIs 0.93%, DIIs 0.38%, Public & Others 42.13% as on 30 June 2026; 137,219,448 outstanding shares.
- [History] Refex Refrigerants Private Limited commenced operations in the refrigerant gas sector in 2002, listed on BSE in 2007, set up a 5 MW solar plant in Rajasthan (2012), renamed Refex Industries Limited (2018), commenced ash and coal handling for thermal power plants, launched RGML mobility operations in Chennai in Sep'23 and incorporated Venwind Refex Power Limited (2024).
